prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1418; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped and struck from behind by a third-party vehicle. Police report requested. Insured reports neck stiffness at the scene but declined transport by EMS. Liability appears clear on preliminary facts pending the report.

Entry 2: Third-party carrier acknowledged the claim and confirmed coverage for its insured driver. Liability accepted in principle. Photos of both vehicles received from the insured; rear bumper damage on the insured vehicle is consistent with the reported impact. Vehicle taken to the preferred repair shop for estimate.

Entry 3: Claimant has retained counsel. All further contact to be routed through the attorney's office. Letter of representation received and logged. Medical authorization requested from counsel. Claimant's prior treatment history requested in the same letter. Reserve adjusted to reflect a bodily injury component.

Entry 4: Attorney's office provided initial treatment records. Diagnosis is cervical strain with whiplash-associated symptoms. Claimant completed a course of physical therapy and reports ongoing headaches and reduced range of motion. Records reviewed. Independent medical examination recommended to verify treatment necessity and causation.

Entry 5: Demand package received from counsel with itemized medical bills, wage loss documentation, and a narrative of ongoing symptoms. Demand is under review by the claims team. Requested a copy of the complete medical file and a recorded statement from the claimant through counsel. Supervisor review scheduled before any response is made.
